_doc: Basics in use: what a new operator needs to know to work with a brain, taught at the moment it is needed. helpers/basics-hint.cjs (UserPromptSubmit) shows at most ONE new basic per session, only when the operator's prompt matches its trigger, and never again once the proof shows the operator used it. A proof is matched against the session's tool calls (their input as JSON), or with "proof_in": "prompt" against the operator's own prompts, or with "both" against either (a skill typed as a slash command is a prompt `<command-name>/…</command-name>`, not a tool call). Triggers are English; an instance adds its language in .claude/rules/basics.json ({"triggers": {"<id>": ["regex", ...]}}) and may add basics of its own ("basics": [...]). Keep the list short — every entry is a sentence the operator reads.

basics.say: To end a session, say "close the session": the AI saves open work, memory and the log, then tells you when you can shut down. Closing the window skips all of that.
Say "autonomously" ("work through it autonomously") and the AI does everything it may decide alone and collects the questions for you; ask "anything for me?" to get them, one by one.
Say "watch" ("keep an eye on the PRs") and the AI arms one watch over pull requests, comments and the shared memory, and handles what arrives by itself.
